title: quran-font-glyphs 1.0
description: For one muṣḥaf: the words its font draws with a single glyph standing for two or more letters and their marks, and whether normalisation changes any drawing under HarfBuzz. Measured by shaping data/mushaf/<key>.json with the font that file names; a view, not a source. The equalities between counts and lists are held by conformance/display_test.py, not by this schema.

generated.description: The dataset's edition date, as in the muṣḥaf file it was measured from.

file.description: The font under data/fonts/, the one the muṣḥaf file's `font` block names.

shaper.description: What turned codepoints into glyphs. The versions are pinned in conformance/requirements.txt.

definition.description: The rule that decides which glyphs are listed, in words.

checked.description: How many words were shaped. conformance/display_test.py holds it equal to the muṣḥaf's word_count.

words_drawn_differently.description: Words whose glyphs or positions change after the named normalisation. Empty means HarfBuzz draws the same picture from the normalised string. It is not a statement about other shapers: see docs/format.md, which says to display the published string untouched.

word_count.description: Distinct words holding at least one listed glyph.

glyphs.description: In the order each glyph first appears in the muṣḥaf.

glyph.description: The glyph's name in the font. KFGQPC's own, quoted.

replaces.description: Every run of plain glyphs the font's GSUB table can build this glyph from, by the font's own glyph names, with a ligature made of ligatures opened down to its plain glyphs. Usually one run.

text.description: The codepoints the glyph was shaped from, as they stand in the words, one string per distinct spelling. A mark the glyph does not take can stand between two it does, so a string is in its word in order but need not be contiguous.

words.description: Positions in the muṣḥaf file's `words`, from 0, ascending. Its length is `word_count`.

assembled_from.description: Present when the glyph is a composite in the font's glyf table: the glyphs it is put together from, so what it shows can be read from them. Absent for a glyph that is an outline of its own.
